data_table.Examination: No palpable neck mass, no bone tenderness, no proximal myopathy, hydration normal
data_table.Investigations: Corrected calcium 2.78 mmol/L (2.10-2.60), parathyroid hormone 6.4 pmol/L (1.6-6.9), phosphate 0.94 mmol/L (0.75-1.50), creatinine 78 micromol/L (60-110), 25-hydroxyvitamin D 68 nmol/L (>50), sestamibi scan shows no definite adenoma, bone mineral density normal for age

lead_in: Which investigation should be performed before any surgical referral proceeds?

options.text: A serum angiotensin converting enzyme level with chest radiography to assess for granulomatous disease
A repeat sestamibi parathyroid scan combined with four dimensional computed tomography imaging
A 24-hour urinary calcium creatinine clearance ratio calculated from paired blood and urine samples
A bone turnover marker panel with repeat bone densitometry performed in twelve months' time
A serum parathyroid hormone related peptide level with computed tomography of the chest and abdomen

subtopic_detail: New central nervous system white matter symptoms arising during biologic therapy for inflammatory arthritis
stem:
You are the rheumatology registrar reviewing a 38-year-old woman who has been taking adalimumab for 14 months for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, with her joints in sustained remission.

For the past three weeks she has had blurred vision in the right eye with pain on eye movement, and she has noticed a band of numbness across her trunk below the ribs. She is afebrile with no headache, no rash and no recent infection. Examination shows reduced visual acuity of 6/18 in the right eye with a right relative afferent pupillary defect and normal fundi, brisk lower limb reflexes and extensor plantar responses. C-reactive protein is 3 mg/L and her full blood count is normal. Her interferon gamma release assay was negative before treatment and she has had no new travel or exposure.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 74/min, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.6 C
data_table.Examination: Right visual acuity 6/18 with relative afferent pupillary defect and normal fundoscopy, sensory level at T8, brisk lower limb reflexes with extensor plantar responses, no joint synovitis, no meningism
data_table.Investigations: C-reactive protein 3 mg/L (<5), full blood count within normal limits, interferon gamma release assay negative before commencing treatment

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Attribute the findings to rheumatoid vasculitis and increase immunosuppression with cyclophosphamide
Cease the biologic agent and arrange urgent neurology review with magnetic resonance imaging
Continue the biologic agent and treat the episode with high dose intravenous methylprednisolone
Switch to a different tumour necrosis factor inhibitor and arrange neurology review as an outpatient
Investigate for opportunistic central nervous system infection and commence empirical antimicrobials

subtopic_detail: Microcytosis with a normal ferritin that has not responded to a long course of oral iron
stem: A 26-year-old woman whose parents were born in Cyprus has taken oral ferrous sulfate daily for 6 months with no improvement in her blood count. Her periods are light. Her father was told he was anaemic and never treated.

data_table.Investigations: Haemoglobin 108 g/L (115-155), mean corpuscular volume 64 fL (80-100), red cell count 5.6 x10^12/L (3.8-5.2), ferritin 85 micrograms/L (30-200)

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Request haemoglobin electrophoresis with chromatography
Give intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and repeat the count
Refer for gastroscopy and colonoscopy for occult blood loss
Switch to alternate day ferrous fumarate for 12 weeks
Insert a levonorgestrel intrauterine system to reduce loss

subtopic_detail: Investigating episodic flushing with diarrhoea and a right sided murmur after normal colonoscopy
stem: A 57-year-old woman has 8 months of flushing of her face and chest lasting 10 minutes, often after red wine and without sweating. She passes five or six loose stools daily and has lost 6 kg.

data_table.Examination: Soft systolic murmur at the left sternal edge louder on inspiration, prominent systolic jugular venous waves, firm liver edge
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid function normal, coeliac serology negative, colonoscopy to terminal ileum normal

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next investigation?

options.text: Serum tryptase with urinary methylhistamine collection
Serum chromogranin A on her current medication
Urinary fractionated metanephrines over 24 hours
Repeat follicle stimulating hormone and oestradiol
Urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid with dietary restriction

subtopic_detail: Heart failure with increased wall thickness and low voltage complexes intolerant of standard therapy
stem: A 78-year-old man has 6 months of exertional breathlessness and ankle swelling. Perindopril and bisoprolol were ceased after his standing systolic fell to 82 mmHg. He has never been hypertensive and had bilateral carpal tunnel releases.

data_table.Investigations: NT-proBNP 4200 ng/L, troponin persistently 48 ng/L without rise or fall
data_table.Imaging: Limb lead QRS under 5 mm; wall thickness 16 mm, ejection fraction 48%, apical sparing on strain

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Invasive coronary angiography for the elevated troponin
Restart bisoprolol at a lower dose and add furosemide
Serum free light chains, urine electrophoresis and bone scintigraphy
Endomyocardial biopsy as the initial definitive investigation
Exercise stress echocardiography for inducible ischaemia

subtopic_detail: Severe abdominal pain with hyponatraemia and proximal weakness after starting a new medication
stem: A 26-year-old woman has 3 days of severe abdominal pain and vomiting, still 9 out of 10 after 20 mg of morphine, with a soft abdomen. She started a combined oral contraceptive pill 4 weeks ago. She is now confused with proximal arm weakness; urine left standing turns reddish brown.

data_table.Investigations: Sodium 118 mmol/L, urine osmolality 480 mmol/kg
data_table.Imaging: Abdominal CT normal

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Restrict fluid to 1 litre daily and recheck sodium
Give 3% saline 100 mL boluses until confusion improves
Arrange diagnostic laparoscopy to find an occult cause
Send urine porphobilinogen and start intravenous haem arginate
Start tolvaptan for presumed inappropriate antidiuretic hormone

subtopic: Palliative and end of life care
subtopic_detail: Responding to a first formal request for voluntary assisted dying in a neurodegenerative illness
stem:
You are a general practitioner in Victoria making a home visit to a 61-year-old man with motor neurone disease, diagnosed 20 months ago. You have been his general practitioner for 12 years.

He now uses non-invasive ventilation overnight and his forced vital capacity is 42 per cent predicted. His neurologist has documented in a recent letter that death is expected within 8 to 10 months. He has an established relationship with the community palliative care service, which has been involved for 6 months.

He has lived in Victoria for the past 8 years and is an Australian citizen. His cognition is intact on formal testing and a recent psychiatric assessment found no depressive disorder and confirmed intact decision-making capacity.

Sitting with his wife present, he tells you clearly and without prompting from anyone: "I want to make a formal request for voluntary assisted dying." You have not completed the approved assessment training. He asks you what happens next.

data_table.Vital signs: Vital signs within normal limits
data_table.Examination: Generalised wasting with fasciculations, uses non-invasive ventilation overnight, forced vital capacity 42 per cent predicted
data_table.Assessment: Cognition intact on formal testing, recent psychiatric assessment found no depressive disorder and confirmed decision-making capacity
data_table.Eligibility details: Australian citizen, resident in Victoria for 8 years, neurologist documents expected death within 8 to 10 months

lead_in: What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Decline the request, because the expected prognosis exceeds the 6 month eligibility limit
Decline the request, because motor neurone disease is specifically excluded from eligibility
Refer him to the palliative care service and revisit this once his prognosis falls under 6 months
Advise that Supreme Court approval must be obtained before any assessment can proceed
Record the request, respond formally within the required period and refer to a trained practitioner

subtopic_detail: Venesection target in a newly diagnosed C282Y homozygote with iron overload
stem:
A 48-year-old man attends your general practice to discuss abnormal blood results. He came in 2 months ago complaining of tiredness and aching in his right hip and in the knuckles at the base of his index and middle fingers on both hands.

He drinks four standard drinks a week, has never injected drugs and takes no supplements or over-the-counter preparations. He has no past history of blood transfusion. His father died at 62 of liver disease that was never fully explained.

His ferritin is 1180 micrograms/L (30-300), transferrin saturation 68 per cent (15-45), alanine aminotransferase 62 U/L (less than 40), C-reactive protein 3 mg/L (less than 5), fasting glucose 5.1 mmol/L (3.0-5.4) and full blood count within normal limits. HFE genotyping reports C282Y homozygosity. Transient elastography gives a liver stiffness of 5.2 kPa, which the report describes as normal.

data_table.Vital signs: Vital signs within normal limits
data_table.Examination: Tenderness of the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally, no hepatomegaly, no skin pigmentation change
data_table.Investigations: Ferritin 1180 micrograms/L (30-300), transferrin saturation 68% (15-45), alanine aminotransferase 62 U/L (less than 40), C-reactive protein 3 mg/L (less than 5), fasting glucose 5.1 mmol/L (3.0-5.4), full blood count within normal limits, HFE C282Y homozygous
data_table.Imaging: Transient elastography liver stiffness 5.2 kPa, reported as normal

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Dietary iron restriction with avoidance of red meat, and repeat ferritin in 6 months
Deferasirox orally with monthly monitoring of renal function and ferritin response
Weekly venesection until the ferritin falls to between 50 and 100 micrograms per litre
Desferrioxamine by subcutaneous infusion five nights a week with ferritin monitoring
Venesection only if a liver biopsy demonstrates established fibrosis on histological staging

subtopic_detail: Treatment of recurrent facial swelling without urticaria unresponsive to adrenaline
stem:
You are the emergency department registrar. A 29-year-old woman presents with swelling of her lower lip and tongue that has developed gradually over the past 6 hours.

This is her third such episode in 2 years. On the previous two occasions she was treated as anaphylaxis and received intramuscular adrenaline, intravenous hydrocortisone and an antihistamine, with no change in the swelling, which resolved over about 3 days each time. She reports no itch and there is no rash anywhere on her body.

She has eaten nothing unusual, has started no new medication and takes no angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor. Her mother has had similar episodes since her twenties and had an emergency laparotomy at 30 for abdominal pain that found nothing.

On examination her tongue and lower lip are swollen, her voice is normal, there is no stridor and she is protecting her own airway. Her C4 level from the last admission was recorded as 0.06 g/L (0.15-0.53). The anaesthetic registrar is aware and the resuscitation bay is prepared.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 92/min, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C
data_table.Examination: Non-pitting swelling of the lower lip and tongue, no urticaria anywhere, no stridor, normal phonation
data_table.Investigations: C4 0.06 g/L (0.15-0.53) recorded at the previous admission

lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Adrenaline 500 micrograms intramuscularly, repeated at 5-minute intervals as needed
Hydrocortisone 200 mg intravenously with promethazine 25 mg given intravenously
Fresh frozen plasma 2 units intravenously with close observation of the airway
C1 esterase inhibitor concentrate intravenously with close observation of the airway
Nebulised adrenaline 5 mg with intravenous dexamethasone and continuous observation

subtopic_detail: Management of a pulmonary exacerbation in an adult with chronic Pseudomonas colonisation
stem:
You are the respiratory registrar in a tertiary adult clinic. A 27-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis attends as a walk-in, having felt progressively worse over 10 days.

She reports that her sputum has doubled in volume and turned dark green, and that she is coughing through the night and has lost 3 kg. She has no fever and no pleuritic pain. She takes a cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator, pancreatic enzyme replacement and inhaled hypertonic saline.

Her best forced expiratory volume in 1 second over the past year was 62 per cent predicted; today it is 48 per cent predicted. Her sputum has repeatedly grown mucoid Pseudomonas aeruginosa over the past 3 years, with sensitivities showing susceptibility to ceftazidime and tobramycin and resistance to ciprofloxacin. Her chest radiograph shows her usual upper lobe bronchiectatic changes without a new consolidation or pneumothorax. Her oxygen saturation is 94 per cent on room air.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 98/min, blood pressure 112/70 mmHg, respiratory rate 20/min, SpO2 94% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C
data_table.Spirometry: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second 48% predicted today, against a best of 62% predicted in the past year
data_table.Microbiology: Repeated mucoid Pseudomonas aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and tobramycin, resistant to ciprofloxacin
data_table.Imaging: Chest radiograph shows established upper lobe bronchiectasis with no new consolidation or pneumothorax

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Oral amoxicillin with clavulanate for 14 days at home with clinic review afterwards
Oral prednisolone 30 mg daily for 7 days with intensified airway clearance at home
Oral ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily for 14 days at home with clinic review afterwards
Nebulised tobramycin alone for a 28-day cycle with clinic review at the end of the course
Admit for intravenous ceftazidime with tobramycin and intensified airway clearance

subtopic_detail: Managing severe obstructive sleep apnoea in a commercial vehicle driver
stem:
A 52-year-old man attends your general practice for the results of a sleep study. He drives a public route bus 5 days a week and holds a commercial vehicle licence.

His wife has complained for years about his snoring and has watched him stop breathing and then gasp. He tells you, once you ask directly, that he has twice nodded off while stopped at traffic lights during his shift, and that he drinks energy drinks to get through the afternoon run.

His body mass index is 34 and his blood pressure today is 152/92 mmHg on no antihypertensive. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale score is 17 out of 24. Laboratory polysomnography reports an apnoea-hypopnoea index of 32 events per hour with a minimum oxygen saturation of 84 per cent and no central events. His thyroid function is normal and his haemoglobin is 158 g/L (130-180). He asks what this means for his job.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 78/min, blood pressure 152/92 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C
data_table.Investigations: Polysomnography apnoea-hypopnoea index 32 events per hour, minimum SpO2 84%, no central events; Epworth Sleepiness Scale 17 out of 24; thyroid function normal; haemoglobin 158 g/L (130-180)
data_table.Examination: Body mass index 34, crowded oropharynx, no goitre

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Start continuous positive airway pressure and advise that he must notify the licensing authority
Fit a mandibular advancement splint and review his daytime sleepiness in 3 months
Recommend a structured weight loss program and repeat the sleep study in 6 months
Start modafinil for his daytime sleepiness and review his Epworth score in 6 weeks
Refer for uvulopalatopharyngoplasty and review his sleep study 3 months after surgery

subtopic_detail: Management of acute bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with erythema nodosum and ankle arthritis
stem: A 34-year-old woman has three weeks of tender nodules on both shins, ten days of painful swollen ankles, a dry cough and evening fevers. She has never smoked.

data_table.Investigations: C-reactive protein 48 mg/L, corrected calcium 2.40 mmol/L, QuantiFERON-TB negative
data_table.Imaging: Chest radiograph shows symmetrical bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with clear lung fields

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Endobronchial ultrasound guided biopsy of the mediastinal nodes
Naproxen with clinical review and repeat imaging in six weeks
Prednisolone 25 mg daily for six weeks with a tapering plan
Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for presumed tuberculosis
Weekly methotrexate with folate and rheumatology review in four weeks

subtopic_detail: Investigating macrocytic anaemia with dysplastic neutrophils and normal haematinics in an older adult
stem: A 73-year-old man has 4 months of tiredness and two falls. He has had no bleeding, black stools or weight loss. There is no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly.

data_table.Investigations: Haemoglobin 92 g/L (130-180), mean corpuscular volume 106 fL, neutrophils 1.2 x10^9/L, platelets 88 x10^9/L, B12, folate and thyroid normal
data_table.Blood film: Hypogranular bilobed neutrophils, no circulating blasts

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Transfuse two units of red cells and recheck in 3 months
Start folic acid and empirical vitamin B12 injections
Refer for bone marrow aspirate and trephine with cytogenetics
Start an erythropoiesis stimulating agent for 8 weeks
Arrange computed tomography for an occult malignancy
